objections.claim: The chosen answer to the shared-classifier question — "import `FAFF_TYPES` from `./native-map` instead of re-literalling the six tokens, so a future taxonomy change cannot leave the two legs disagreeing about what the types are" — is overstated by the spec's own design. The classifier's actual mapping lives in `CLASSIFIER_TABLE`, whose keys are the five substantive type tokens written as literals; importing the enum covers only set membership, not the mapping. A taxonomy rename or addition still requires hand-editing the table, at which point the two legs can disagree exactly as before. The DONE item compounds this: "the module contains no literal list of the six" is unachievable as written — the table keys are literal type tokens, and the bad-enum usage message (which the spec says must match `native-map get`'s `Accepted: bug, feature, …` wording) needs the six names too.
objections.evidence: "Design decision — share a classifier with the Linear leg…" (`**Chosen:**` paragraph); `CLASSIFIER_TABLE` table in HOW; DONE item "The six faff-type tokens appear in the module only via `FAFF_TYPES`…".
objections.predicted_consequence: A builder either fails the literal reading of the DONE item, or satisfies it vacuously while the claimed drift-closure never existed — the first taxonomy change silently desynchronises the GitHub table from the Linear leg, the exact failure the decision was made to prevent.

objections.claim: The slice ships a candidate set whose only consumer is FAFF-1113; until that sibling lands, the scan runs for nobody. The critique itself names this ("FAFF-1112 on its own lights up no observable end-user value") and recommends only that FAFF-1113 "belong adjacent in the build queue" — a recommendation with no mechanism behind it, so the sequencing consequence is left to queue discipline rather than a dependency edge or a plot-level constraint.
objections.evidence: Methodology critique, "Sequencing consequence worth naming (principle 2)"; spec's own OUT OF SCOPE entry deferring the scorer/selection verb to FAFF-1113.
objections.predicted_consequence: FAFF-1112 clears review, lands, and sits unused while unrelated work interleaves before FAFF-1113 — the accepted cost of the right-sizing split becomes an unbounded one, and the scan's registration cost (six points, two lint-enforced) is paid for a verb with zero reachable consumers in the interim.

objections.claim: The DONE item "The six faff-type tokens appear in the module only via `FAFF_TYPES` imported from `./native-map`; the module contains no literal list of the six" cannot be satisfied by the classifier the same spec mandates: `CLASSIFIER_TABLE`'s rows are keyed by the literal tokens `bug`, `spike`, `chore`, `epic`, `feature` — five faff-type tokens appearing as literals in the module, outside any `FAFF_TYPES` import. A tester applying the criterion as written must fail every conforming build; a builder reading it as intended ("don't re-literal the taxonomy *array*") passes. The criterion is decidable but self-contradictory, so its pass/fail line is not the one the spec means.
objections.evidence: DONE item under "### From WHAT (types and interfaces)" vs the `CLASSIFIER_TABLE` in "### HOW — Behaviour".
objections.predicted_consequence: the build's own DONE checklist contains an item that is mechanically false for the mandated implementation — either the criterion is silently ignored (dead AC) or a correct build is failed against it; neither outcome verifies what the criterion was written to prevent (taxonomy drift between the two legs).
